report_name: Malicious 'indexed-btree' NPM Package Amasses Millions of Downloads

threat_actors.name: charlessadler25
threat_actors.description: The threat actor handle that published the malicious 'indexed-btree' npm package, using runtime evasion and blockchain for C2 to generate over €230,000.
threat_actors.goals: Financial profit through widespread distribution of an infostealing malware package.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The attacker published a malicious package named 'indexed-btree' to the public npm repository, which was then downloaded and integrated into countless downstream projects.

attack_patterns.name: Execution Guardrails
attack_patterns.description: The malicious payload was hidden within a standard runtime function (BTree.prototype.set()) instead of common install scripts, ensuring it only executed when the function was actively used in a downstream application, thus bypassing install-time security scanners.

attack_patterns.name: System Information Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The first-stage loader performed host fingerprinting, collecting OS details, architecture, and hostname.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: Collected system data was exfiltrated to a hardcoded Slack channel and Telegram bot, using legitimate web services for C2 and exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The malware used a novel C2 technique called "EtherHiding," querying a smart contract on the Sepolia Ethereum testnet to retrieve the encrypted second-stage payload, making the C2 infrastructure highly resilient.

attack_patterns.name: File Deletion
attack_patterns.description: After executing the second stage, the malware attempted to delete its traces from the system.

attack_patterns.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The malicious loader was embedded within a standard runtime function, remaining dormant and hidden from static analysis until triggered by application use.

malware.name: indexed-btree
malware.description: A malicious npm package that masqueraded as a data structure utility. It used runtime execution to evade detection, fingerprint hosts, exfiltrate data via Slack/Telegram, and used the Ethereum blockchain for its second-stage C2.

tools.name: Slack
tools.description: Used as a C2 and data exfiltration channel for the first stage of the attack via a hardcoded webhook.

tools.name: Telegram
tools.description: Used as a C2 and data exfiltration channel for the first stage of the attack via a hardcoded bot.

identities.name: npm
identities.description: The public package repository where the malicious 'indexed-btree' package was hosted, achieving nearly two million weekly downloads before removal.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: Used to host a fabricated repository with a plausible commit history to make the malicious 'indexed-btree' package appear legitimate.

identities.name: Developers
identities.description: The primary victims of the attack, who integrated the malicious 'indexed-btree' package into their downstream projects.

infrastructure.name: Slack/Telegram Exfiltration Channel
infrastructure.description: Hardcoded Slack webhook and Telegram bot API endpoints used for initial data exfiltration and C2.

infrastructure.name: EtherHiding C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A novel C2 mechanism using a smart contract on the Sepolia Ethereum testnet to store and retrieve the encrypted second-stage payload.

indicators.name: Suspicious C2 and Exfiltration Domain Queries
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Suspicious C2 and Exfiltration Domain Queries for indexed-btree
id: 2b3a1c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-0123456789ab
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to domains associated with Slack webhooks, Telegram bots, and Ethereum gateways, which were used by the malicious 'indexed-btree' npm package for C2 and exfiltration.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/malicious-npm-package-indexed-btree-hid.html
tags:
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.t1102
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'hooks.slack.com'
      - 'api.telegram.org'
      - 'sepolia.infura.io'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries to domains used for C2 and exfiltration by the 'indexed-btree' malware.

indicators.name: Suspicious Inline Node.js Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Inline Node.js Execution
id: 8f7e6d5c-4b3a-4987-6543-fedcba987654
status: experimental
description: Detects Node.js being used to execute obfuscated inline scripts, a technique that can be used by malicious packages like 'indexed-btree' to run their payload.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/malicious-npm-package-indexed-btree-hid.html
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\node.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' -e '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Node.js executing an inline script, which may indicate a malicious package like 'indexed-btree' is running its payload.

indicators.name: Malicious NPM Package 'indexed-btree' File Presence
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Malicious NPM Package 'indexed-btree' File Presence
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-fedcba987654
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of the malicious 'indexed-btree' npm package directory within the node_modules folder.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/malicious-npm-package-indexed-btree-hid.html
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.initial_access
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\node_modules\indexed-btree\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the malicious 'indexed-btree' package directory.
